rules.name: Acts on the live product
rules.statement: A command is a way in only when it acts on the running product or its stored data.
rules.risk: A build or test command counted as a way in makes the outside edge look wider than it is.

sites.why: States the only test that decides a command: what the command acts on, not its name and not its purpose.
Hands the same test to the agent that mints the way-in rows. A table shows what counts on each side.

rules.name: Moved out, still written down
rules.statement: A command judged not to be a way in must still be recorded as a run or build command.
rules.risk: A command decided against and never rewritten disappears from the map. No check can see a row nobody wrote.

sites.why: Says the decision is only half the work. The other half is writing the command into the run-and-build list.
Makes the mover count and name every command it took out, so the second half becomes visible in the reply.

rules.name: One way in at the acting command
rules.statement: A way in is recorded once, at the thing that does the acting, and never again at whatever calls it.
rules.risk: Counting a wrapper and the command it wraps as two doors inflates the outside edge with duplicate rows.

sites.why: Says a command calling one of the product's own addresses adds no new way in. The address already is one.
Says a wrapper and the command it wraps are one way in, recorded at the command that acts.
States both cuts in the method itself, so the rule survives outside the worker brief.

rules.name: Self-started work is not a way in
rules.statement: A timer, a boot hook or a queue reader is work the product does to itself, not a way in.
rules.risk: Placing the product's own scheduled work on the outside edge makes it look reachable where nobody outside can reach it.

sites.why: Rejects an interface that claims a self-started way in, and says the work is the product acting on itself.
Keeps only the outside-driven ways in, so every outside-edge check reads the same shorter list.
Fixes, per kind of way in, which ones are self-started and which ones somebody outside asks for.

rules.name: Unknown kind counts as outside-driven
rules.statement: A way in of a kind nobody recognises is treated as one somebody outside asks for.
rules.risk: Guessing self-started instead would quietly drop a real door out of every count of the outside edge.

sites.why: Answers outside-driven whenever no self-starting word matches the kind of the way in.

rules.name: One way in, exactly one interface
rules.statement: Every way in that somebody outside asks for belongs to exactly one interface, or its absence is recorded.
rules.risk: A way in claimed twice, or by nothing, breaks any honest count of where the product meets the world.

sites.why: States the one-interface rule and the recorded line that excuses a deliberate exception.
Blocks a way in that more than one interface claims, and blocks one interface listing it twice.
Collects the ways in that no interface claims and that no recorded line excuses.

rules.name: Shared request handling is not a way in
rules.statement: Work every request passes through on its way in is not itself a way in, so it joins no interface.
rules.risk: Demanding an interface for shared request handling raises a complaint nobody can ever clear, so readers stop reading complaints.

sites.why: Names shared request handling as the one kind excused from belonging to an interface.
Drops that kind before every check that asks which interface a way in belongs to.

rules.name: Every way in owes a story
rules.statement: A way in that no story reaches is reported, including the ones the product starts for itself.
rules.risk: Exempting scheduled work hides a whole background behaviour, with no signal anywhere that it is missing.

sites.why: States that self-started ways in are not exempt, because a scheduled job is an actor with a goal.
Reports the outside-driven ways in that no story reaches, grouped by the part of the product that owns them.
Reports the self-started ways in that no story reaches, in the same grouped shape.
